Royal-official / chamberlain / eunuch (Gen 37:36; 39:1; 40:2,7; 1Sa 8:15; 1Ki 22:9; 2Ki 8:6; 9:32; 18:17 (variant); 20:18; 23:11; 24:12,15; 25:19; 1Chr 28:1; 2Chr 18:8; Esth 1:10,12,15; 2:3,14,15,21; 4:4,5; 6:2,14; 7:9; Isa 39:7; 56:3,4; Jer 29:2; 34:19; 38:7; 41:16; 52:25; Dan 1:3,7-11,18). 42 occurrences. Hyphenated. The Hebrew is ambiguous between castrated-officials (Esth 2:3; Isa 56:3-5) and the broader court-officer (Gen 37:36, where Potiphar is married). Concordant 'court-official' preserves the broader sense; KJV 'eunuch' is too specific.

The major OT-noun for servant / slave / vassal (Gen 9:25-27; 12:16; 14:15; 17:12,13,23,27; 18:3,5,17 (variant); 19:2,19; 20:8,14; 21:25; 24:2-65; 26:15,19,24,25,32; 27:37; 30:43; 32:5,11,17,19,21; 33:5,14; 39:17,19; 40:20; 41:10,37,38; 42:10-13; 43:18,28; 44:7-33; 45:16; 47:3,4,19,25; 50:2,7,17,18; etc.). 796 occurrences. Standard. The most-frequent servant-noun. Distinguished from H8334 sharath-Pi (minister-priestly), H5288 naar (lad/young-servant), H6800 tsanaph (bond-servant rare), H5650 covers slave (Ex 21:2-32), royal-servant (1Sa 16:15-22), worship-servant ('servants of YH', Pss 113:1; 134:1), and the messianic 'Servant of YH' (Isa 42:1; 49:3; 52:13).
Used (Jdg 9:26-31; Ezr 8:6). 6 occurrences. Means 'servant'. English convention.
